intervention.description: CALPHAD-based high-throughput computational method to design alloys

evidence_spans: Through the high-throughput screening, precipitation-strengthened lightweight high-entropy alloys are discovered from thousands of initial compositions, which exhibit enhanced strengths compared to other counterparts at room and elevated temperatures.

intervention.description: Heating the alloy to elevated temperatures to observe phase stability and order-disorder transitions

structure.description: Coexistence of BCC and L21 phases at temperatures below 900 °C

evidence_units.mechanism: The L21 phase remains stable and coexists with the BCC phase up to 900 °C; the relative intensity of superstructure peaks decreases upon heating due to the reduced fraction of the L21 phase, indicating a transition towards disorder or phase dissolution

outcome.measurement_method: In situ neutron scattering (detection of unique L21 peaks)

evidence_spans: As shown in Fig. 4a for Alloy 1, the unique L2 1 peaks (highlighted by the green color) are observed only at 900 °C and below, indicating that L2 1 is stable up to 900 °C, below which both the BCC and L2 1 phases coexist.
The relative intensity of superstructure peaks for the L2 1 phase decreases upon heating, which is due to the reduced fraction of the L2 1 phase.

This prediction is consistent with the experimental observations (Fig. 4 a, b ), i.e., Alloy 1 is composed of L2 1 and BCC phases from RT to 900 °C, while only the ordered L2 1 phase still exists in Alloy 7 from RT to 1050 °C.

intervention.description: Simulation of partial pair distribution functions (PDF) to analyze atomic bonding preferences in the molten state

structure.description: Molten state with specific pair correlation intensities indicating bonding tendencies

evidence_units.mechanism: Strong pair correlations between Al-Fe and Cr-Fe in the molten state suggest that these interactions promote the formation of L21 and BCC phases upon solidification

outcome.measurement_method: Ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) simulation of partial PDFs

evidence_spans: Ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) simulations were also performed on Alloy 1 in its molten state to support the MC-calculation results.
Figure 5a–e shows the selected partial PDF of Alloy 1 at T = 1600 °C to the first nearest neighbor.

The intensities of pair correlations of the Al–Al and Ti–Ti bonds are significantly lower than the other pair correlations, indicating the strong tendency for Al and Ti atoms to bond with other elements.
On the other hand, the Al–Fe pair correlation has the highest intensity, and the Cr–Fe pair correlation has the second-highest intensity, compared to other pair correlations.

The persistent presence of stronger Al–Fe and Cr–Fe pair correlations in the Al–Cr–Fe–Mn–Ti alloys suggests that Al–Fe and Cr–Fe pair interactions may promote the formation of L2 1 and BCC phases, respectively, as evidenced by the chemical compositions of both phases (Table 1 ).

intervention.description: Room temperature compression to evaluate yield strength

structure.description: BCC matrix with high-density nanoscaled L21 precipitates
microstructure: Nanoscale L21 precipitates (10-30 nm, ~39 nm after annealing)

evidence_units.mechanism: Precipitation strengthening driven by load transfer to the hard L21 phase and ordering strengthening contribution

comparison.direction: Higher (Alloy 1 yield strength ~1642 MPa vs G2 ~500-800 MPa range implied by comparison to 1072 MPa)

evidence_spans: To evaluate the mechanical properties of the identified eight alloys in a high-throughput manner, we performed compression tests on the eight alloys at room temperature (RT) (Fig. 3a ).
Alloys 1 and 8 exhibit high yield strengths below 700 °C (1072 ± 25 MPa at 600 °C for Alloy 1; 1032 ± 10 MPa at 600 °C for Alloy 8).

The precipitation-strengthening contribution in Alloy 1 is quantitatively calculated (Supplementary Note 1), which is mainly attributed to the ordering strengthening (~904 MPa), close to the yield strength differences between Alloys 1 and 2 (~874 MPa), and between Alloys 1 and 7 (~860 MPa).

One can notice that Alloy 1 displays a clear load-transfer behavior upon the BCC phase yielding (around 1000 MPa), i.e., the hard L2 1 phase bears a larger load with greater lattice strains (L2 1 {222} and {420}), while the soft BCC phase undertakes a lower load with lower lattice strains (BCC {110} and {211}), which is a reflection of the precipitation strengthening.
limitations: Number density of precipitates highly underestimated due to touching/overlapping precipitates

intervention.description: Measurement of lattice strain under applied stress to detect load transfer

structure.description: Ordered L21 antiphase domains (APDs) with thin film of disordered BCC at boundaries, acting as a single phase

evidence_units.mechanism: Synchronized response of various hkl-specific lattice strains indicates behavior like a single L21 phase without load transfer
evidence_spans: In contrast, no load transfer was observed in Alloy 7 (Fig. 3d ).
The synchronized response of various hkl -specific lattice strains versus applied stress indicates that Alloy 7 behaves like a single L2 1 phase.
Therefore, the high yield strengths of Alloys 1 and 8 are attributed to the precipitation strengthening, besides the effect of atomic-level complexity in HEAs.

material.name: Al–Cr–Fe–Mn–Ti quinary system
material.composition: composition range of 5–50 at.% for each element

intervention.description: Screening of potential alloys using CALPHAD method with a step size of 10 at.%

evidence_units.mechanism: Computational software efficiency allows massive calculations to be completed rapidly, enabling the screening of a vast compositional space.

comparison.baseline_state: using a step size of 1 at.%

evidence_spans: In the example of the Al–Cr–Fe–Mn–Ti quinary system, it takes only a few hours on a desktop computer to finish the HTCs (~ 3 × 10 3 ) within the composition range of 5–50 at.% for each element and finally screen out eight potential alloys. However, if a step size of 1 at.% for this quinary system is used, the computational time will easily increase to a few thousands of hours, posing a challenge for a single personal computer.

material.name: Al–Cr–Fe–Mn–Ti quinary system
material.composition: composition range of 5–50 at.% for each element

intervention.description: Screening with step size of 10 at.%

evidence_units.mechanism: Rapid computation allows for the identification of potential alloys from a vast compositional space.
evidence_spans: In the example of the Al–Cr–Fe–Mn–Ti quinary system, it takes only a few hours on a desktop computer to finish the HTCs (~ 3 × 10 3 ) within the composition range of 5–50 at.% for each element and finally screen out eight potential alloys. However, if a step size of 1 at.% for this quinary system is used, the computational time will easily increase to a few thousands of hours, posing a challenge for a single personal computer. The computational time will be scaled up substantially with higher-order systems (the number of components > 5).
limitations: Computational time scales up substantially with higher-order systems (the number of components > 5).

intervention.description: Prediction of microstructure based on current thermodynamic database

structure.description: microstructure discrepancy between prediction and observation

evidence_units.mechanism: Inaccuracies in the thermodynamic database lead to discrepancies in the predicted stability of the L2 1 phase.
evidence_spans: The microstructure discrepancy between the thermodynamic prediction and experimental observation indicates that our current thermodynamic database needs further improvement on the stability of the L2 1 phase.
Our results on the discovered LWHEAs demonstrate the sensitivity of the nanoscaled L2 1 precipitates-strengthened BCC microstructure to alloys’ chemical compositions.
limitations: Current thermodynamic database needs further improvement on the stability of the L2 1 phase.

material.name: LWHEAs
material.composition: Al < 25 at.% and Mn > 15 at.% with the unchanged contents of other elements

intervention.description: Prediction valid within specific composition range

evidence_units.mechanism: The microstructure is sensitive to chemical compositions related to the critical ordering temperature and morphology of L2 1 precipitates.
evidence_spans: Our results on the discovered LWHEAs demonstrate the sensitivity of the nanoscaled L2 1 precipitates-strengthened BCC microstructure to alloys’ chemical compositions. Therefore, the scrutiny of the alloys’ chemical compositions that are related to the critical ordering temperature and morphology of L2 1 precipitates is required during alloy design. However, the current high-throughput predictions are valid in the composition range of Al < 25 at.% and Mn > 15 at.% with the unchanged contents of other elements.
limitations: Current high-throughput predictions are valid only in the composition range of Al < 25 at.% and Mn > 15 at.% with the unchanged contents of other elements.

intervention.description: 2000-atom supercells with 10^7 MC steps within nearest-neighbor interaction approximation to calculate short-range and long-range ordering parameters

structure.description: Order-disorder transition behavior characterized by LRO and SRO parameters
microstructure: L21 nanoscale precipitates in BCC matrix

candidate.mechanism: Al, Cr, and Ti segregate to one sublattice while Fe and Mn occupy the other; Fe-Al and Fe-Ti pairs promote L21 formation, while Cr-Fe pairs promote BCC formation; the ordering transition temperature (Tc) is determined by the relative strength of these interactions and stoichiometry

outcome.measurement_method: Metropolis Monte Carlo (MC) calculation of LRO parameters

evidence_spans: We further conducted the metropolis Monte Carlo (MC) calculations to understand the order-disorder transitions in Alloys 1 and 7 during solidification, using much larger supercells of 2000 atoms at 10 7 MC steps within the nearest-neighbor interaction approximation.

The LRO can be expressed as [32] where y i α and y i β are the site occupancy of the element, i , on sublattices, α and β , respectively. The value of η i falls within the range of −1 to 1, as shown in Fig. 4 c, d.
When η i = 0 , the element, i , is randomly distributed on both α and β sublattices. When η i equals 1 or −1, the element, i , can be exclusively found on the α or β sublattice.

The order-disorder transition can be directly reflected by the LRO parameters (Fig. 4 c, d ). In both Alloys 1 and 7, as the temperature decreases, Al, Cr, and Ti tend to segregate to one sublattice, while Fe and Mn primarily occupy the other.

As indicated by the red arrows, the ordering transition temperature, T c , of Alloy 1 [1607 °C (1880 K)] is much lower than that of Alloy 7 [1997 °C (2270 K), far beyond its melting temperature], suggesting that the ordered L2 1 phase is less easily retained in the solid state in Alloy 1 than in Alloy 7 [33] .
